extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism ontology; in silico docking is kept separate from direct antiviral phenotype.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Synthetic SS-I inhibits SARS-CoV-2 infection in Vero CCL-81 cells with EC50 2.7 uM.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: linear synthetic SS-I peptide used in biological assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: Phenotypic antiviral activity does not by itself prove the docking-predicted ACE2/spike mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Docking and MD simulations hypothesize SS-I contacts with ACE2 and SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD, but the paper states in vitro structural interaction is not established.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: homology-predicted SS-I structure in computational complexes
mechanism_claims.limitations: No NMR, crystallography, binding biophysics, or infection-entry mechanism assay is reported for the peptide-protein interaction.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SS-I has high hemolytic activity; the paper discusses hydrophobic membrane interaction as a plausible toxicity context, not a direct molecular mechanism assay.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: linear synthetic SS-I peptide in human erythrocyte assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Membrane-disruption mechanism is inferred from hemolysis and literature context, not directly measured for SS-I.

source_review_summary.overclaim_screen: No ACE2/spike direct mechanism is promoted from docking/MD alone.
